pages.title: Home
pages.description: The Bible tells one story. These pages tell it more than once, each time from a different angle.

headings.name: One story

columns.text: The Bible tells one story. It starts in a garden 1 and ends with the tree of life by the river of life. 2 In between there is a rebellion in heaven 3 and on earth, 4 a scattering of nations, 5 a people chosen, 6 a Son sent, 7 and a family gathered. 8
1 Gen 2:8 2 Rev 22:1-2 3 Jude 6 4 Gen 3:6 5 Gen 11:9 6 Deu 7:6 7 Gal 4:4 8 Eph 1:10

headings.name: Told more than once

columns.text:
These pages tell that story four times, each from a different angle. Sons of God follows God's family in heaven and on earth. Fall and Restoration follows creation, the break and the repair. Reversals sets each loss beside what is given back. The Feasts of Yahweh follows the calendar God gave Israel.

Each page stands on its own and runs from Genesis to Revelation, so you can read them in any order.

headings.name: Read them side by side

columns.text: Read one, then another, and notice where they meet.

headings.name: How to read

columns.text: Each step of the story carries a numbered footnote with one Scripture reference, so the story reads straight through. Open the verses and check them. Where a line draws a conclusion the verses do not state in so many words, the text says so, as an Inference. Yahweh is God's own name. 1  Most English Bibles, including the NKJV, print it as LORD in capitals. These pages use the name itself where the Hebrew has it.
1 Exo 3:15

pages.title: Paradise of God: Restored

headings.name: Introduction

columns.text: This whole Bible story in three parts. In the first part, God creates a good world and a home where people can live with Him. In the second part, people turn away from God, and the world and its people are broken. In the third part, God repairs what was broken and comes to live with His people forever. The story begins before the world existed, with God's purpose.

headings.name: Paradise

columns.text: Before God made anything, He already had a purpose. He wanted to live among His people and be their God. 2 God also knew that people would sin, and that their sin would separate them from Him. 3 So, before He made the world, God planned a way to bring them back to Himself: a perfect, spotless sacrifice to deal with their sin. The apostle Peter explains that God chose Christ for this sacrifice before the world was made, and that Christ was revealed in these last times, the final age that began when Christ came. 4
2 Eph 1:4-5 Lev 26:12 3 Isa 59:2 4 1Pe 1:19-20

Then God started by creating. God spoke, and light came into being. 1  God planted a garden in a place called Eden, put the first man, Adam, there, and set the tree of life in the middle of the garden. 2  Whoever ate from the tree of life would live forever. 3  God gave Adam and his wife, Eve, rule over the earth and told them to have children and fill the earth. God looked at everything He had made and saw that it was very good. 4  People lived with God, and the world was whole.
1 Gen 1:3 2 Gen 2:8-9 3 Gen 3:22 4 Gen 1:28-31

headings.name: The Fall

columns.text: God gave Adam one rule. Adam could eat from any tree in the garden except the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and God warned that if Adam ate from that tree he would surely die. 1  Adam and Eve ate from that tree, and then they hid from God, whose personal name is Yahweh. 2  Yahweh God sent Adam out of the garden, away from the tree of life. 3  The ground was cursed and grew thorns and thistles, and people would have to work hard for their food until they died and their bodies returned to the dust. 4  This is the break that the rest of the story sets out to repair. People were shut out from God's presence, and death had entered the world.
1 Gen 2:17 2 Gen 3:6-8 3 Gen 3:23-24 4 Gen 3:17-19

The break spread. Adam's son Cain murdered his brother Abel. 1  Heavenly beings called the sons of God took wives from among women on earth, 2 and the earth was filled with violence. 3  Yahweh sent a great flood on the earth, though He saved Noah and his family. 4  After the Flood, people at a place called Babel built a tower to make a name for themselves, so that they would not be scattered over the earth. 5  Yahweh scattered them across the whole earth anyway. 6
1 Gen 4:8 2 Gen 6:2 3 Gen 6:11 4 Gen 7:1-4 5 Gen 11:4 6 Gen 11:8

paragraphs.title: A nation, and a nation exiled

columns.text: God then made a fresh start with one family. Yahweh chose the descendants of a man named Abraham to be His own people, the nation of Israel. 1  Yahweh came down on Mount Sinai in fire and met with Israel there. 2  Yahweh told Israel to build a tabernacle, a large tent, so that He could live among them. 3  Yahweh's presence stayed in the innermost room, behind a veil. 4  Only the high priest could go behind the veil, only once a year, and never without the blood of a sacrifice, an animal killed to cover the people's sins. 5  Later a permanent temple in Jerusalem took the place of the tent. So God lived among His people again, but sin still kept them at a distance. Israel kept turning to idols. 6  The glory of Yahweh, the visible sign of His presence, left the temple, 7 and the people were taken away into exile in Babylon. 8
1 Deu 7:6 2 Exo 19:18 3 Exo 25:8 4 Lev 16:2 5 Heb 9:7 6 Ezk 8:10 7 Ezk 10:18 8 2Ki 25:11

headings.name: Paradise Restored

columns.text: Then the repair began. In Eden, God had promised that a Seed, a descendant of the woman, would crush the serpent. 1  At the time God had set, the promised Seed was born of a woman. 2  The promised Seed was Jesus, the Son of God, who became a human being and lived among people. 3  Jesus faced every kind of temptation people face, yet Jesus never sinned. 4  Passover was the night in Egypt when the blood of a lamb protected Israel's homes from death. Jesus died as the Passover lamb, the sacrifice God had planned before creation. 5  Jesus rose from the dead as the firstfruits, the first of everyone God will raise. 6  When Jesus died, the veil in the temple, the curtain that kept people out of God's presence, was torn in two. 7  The way back to God was open.
1 Gen 3:15 2 Gal 4:4 3 Jhn 1:14 4 Heb 4:15 5 1Co 5:7 6 1Co 15:20 7 Mat 27:51

The story is not finished yet. The prophet Zechariah saw Yahweh coming with all His holy ones. 1  Revelation shows Christ, the King God promised, coming to judge and fight with justice. 2  Christ will bind the serpent of old, the Devil, 3 and God will bring the people of Israel back into their own land. 4  Christ will reign for a thousand years, 5 the nations will learn Yahweh's ways, 6 and the whole earth will know Yahweh as fully as water fills the sea. 7
1 Zec 14:5 2 Rev 19:11 3 Rev 20:2 4 Ezk 37:21 5 Rev 20:4 6 Isa 2:3 7 Isa 11:9

When every enemy, including death, has been put under Christ's feet, Christ hands the kingdom to God the Father. 1  A new city, the New Jerusalem, comes down out of heaven to a renewed earth, and God makes His home with people. 2  The curse that began in Eden is gone, God's servants see God's face, and the tree of life stands again. 3  The serpent is gone for good. 4  What God purposed before creation has come true: God lives among His people as their God.
1 1Co 15:24-26 2 Rev 21:1-3 3 Rev 22:2-4 4 Rev 20:10

pages.contentsNote: God dwelt with Mankind until they rebelled. God will return so that they may once again dwell in Paradise with God.

pages.title: Sons of God: Family of Yahweh

headings.name: Two families of the sons of God

columns.text: This page tells the story of God's family, from the beginning of the Bible to the end. The Bible uses the phrase sons of God for two groups. The first group is heavenly beings who stand in God's presence. 1 The second group is people on earth whom God takes as His own children. 2 The story follows both groups. Some of the heavenly sons of God rebel, the first son of God on earth falls, and God then works through history to gather a family that will live with Him forever. Before God made the world, God had already chosen a people to become His sons. 3 When God laid the foundations of the earth, the heavenly sons of God shouted for joy. 4 God then formed the first man, Adam, and the Gospel of Luke calls Adam a son of God. 5 So God had one family of sons in heaven and the beginning of another on earth. God's plan was to bring His whole family in heaven and on earth together under Christ. 6
1 Job 1:6 2 Gal 3:26 3 Eph 1:4-5 4 Job 38:4-7 5 Luk 3:38 6 Eph 1:10

headings.name: Eden: a son of God and the serpent rebel

columns.text: God, whose personal name is Yahweh, placed Adam in a garden called Eden to work it and look after it. 1  A serpent in the garden contradicted God and told the woman, Eve, that eating the fruit of the one forbidden tree would make her like God. Eve ate the fruit, Adam ate it too, and both of them hid from Yahweh God. 2  Yahweh sent Adam and Eve out of the garden, and heavenly guards called cherubim blocked the way back to the tree of life. 3  So the first son of God on earth lost his home with God. Yahweh did not leave the matter there. Yahweh told the serpent that a Seed, a descendant of the woman, would one day crush the serpent's head, while the serpent would wound the Seed's heel. 4  The book of Revelation later names the serpent as the Devil, also called Satan. 5  The apostle Paul says the promised Seed is Christ, who was born of a woman. 6  Genesis itself does not name the Seed, so the reader has to wait for the rest of the story.
1 Gen 2:15 2 Gen 3:5-8 3 Gen 3:23-24 4 Gen 3:15 5 Rev 12:9 6 Gal 3:16 Gal 4:4

headings.name: The Flood: the sons of God rebel

columns.text: As the number of people on earth grew, the heavenly sons of God saw the daughters of men and took any of them they wanted as wives. 1  Genesis tells this in only a few words. The apostle Peter adds that some angels sinned and that God cast those angels down into darkness to wait for judgement. 2  Jude adds that some angels left the place God had given them. 3  Neither Peter nor Jude names Genesis 6, so linking their words to Genesis 6 is a conclusion drawn from the verses. In those days giants lived on the earth, and Yahweh saw that people thought about nothing but evil, all the time. 4  God sent a great flood on the world that had turned against Him, but God saved Noah and his family. 5  :::info Who are the sons of God? In Job the phrase sons of God is used of heavenly beings. Job 1:6 Job 2:1 Job 38:7 Genesis 6 uses it of those who took wives from the daughters of men. Many Christians read these sons of God as men of Seth’s line instead. Gen 6:2 Gen 6:4 In Deuteronomy 32:8 the ESV follows a Dead Sea Scroll and the Septuagint. It says God fixed the borders of the nations according to the number of the sons of God. Deu 32:8 In the New Testament the title belongs to those led by the Spirit and to all who believe. Rom 8:14 Gal 3:26
1 Gen 6:1-2 2 2Pe 2:4 3 Jude 6 4 Gen 6:4-5 5 2Pe 2:5

headings.name: Babel: the nations are given to the sons of God

columns.text: After the Flood, people gathered on a plain and began to build a city with a tower, so that they could make a name for themselves. 1  Yahweh confused their language so that they could no longer understand one another, and Yahweh scattered them over the whole earth. 2  Moses later sang that the Most High gave each scattered nation its land and set the borders of the nations by the number of the sons of God, but Yahweh kept the people of Jacob, Israel, as His own. 3  The ESV, an English translation, reads "sons of God" in this verse, following a Dead Sea Scroll and the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament. The NKJV follows the standard Hebrew text, which reads "children of Israel". Moses warned Israel not to worship the host of heaven, which Yahweh had given to the other nations. 4  So the other nations were handed over to lesser powers, and only Israel was kept as Yahweh's own. Later in the story the nations are brought back.
1 Gen 11:4 2 Gen 11:9 3 Deu 32:8-9 4 Deu 4:19

headings.name: God creates His own nation of sons

columns.text: Yahweh then began to build a family of sons on earth. Yahweh called a man named Abraham and promised that every family on earth would be blessed through him. 1  Abraham's descendants became the nation of Israel. After Israel had been slaves in Egypt, Yahweh brought them out and told them that they would be His own treasured people and a nation of priests, 2 a people who worshipped no other god. 3  Even so, Israel turned away from Yahweh and offered sacrifices, animals killed as gifts of worship, to demons and to foreign gods. 4  Because of this, the glory of Yahweh, the visible sign of His presence, left the temple in Jerusalem. 5  The northern kingdom of Israel was taken captive to Assyria, 6 and the southern kingdom of Judah was later taken captive to Babylon. 7  God's family of sons on earth had failed, just as Adam had failed.
1 Gen 12:1-3 2 Exo 19:5-6 3 Exo 20:3 4 Deu 32:17 5 Ezk 10:18 6 2Ki 17:6 7 2Ki 25:11

headings.name: The sons of God are judged

columns.text: While God's sons on earth failed, the heavenly powers over the nations failed too. Psalm 82 describes a scene in heaven. God takes His place in the congregation of the mighty, an assembly of heavenly beings, and judges the gods there. 1  The word for God here is Elohim in Hebrew, not Yahweh. God calls these gods sons of the Most High, yet tells them that they will die like men. The psalm ends by asking God to rise up and judge the earth, because all the nations belong to God. 2  So the heavenly sons of God who were given the nations at Babel will lose them, and the nations will return to God.
1 Psa 82:1 2 Psa 82:6-8

headings.name: The Son of God brings many sons

columns.text: Then the promised Seed came. The Son of God was born as a human being, and people saw His glory as the Father's only Son. 1  This Son is Jesus, also called Christ, a title that means the anointed one, the King God had promised. God's aim was to bring many sons to glory. God made Jesus perfect through suffering, and Jesus is glad to call those sons His brothers. 2  The Son of God came to undo the Devil's work. 3  When Jesus died on the cross, He stripped the ruling spiritual powers of their weapons. 4  The serpent's end is now certain. God will soon crush Satan under the feet of God's people, 5 and the Devil will finally be thrown into the lake of fire. 6  The promise made in Eden, that the Seed would crush the serpent's head, is being kept.
1 Jhn 1:14 2 Heb 2:10-11 3 1Jn 3:8 4 Col 2:15 5 Rom 16:20 6 Rev 20:10

headings.name: Adopted sons of God

columns.text: What Adam lost, Christ gives back. Everyone who receives Christ is given the right to become a child of God. 1  All who believe are sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus, and in Christ it makes no difference whether a person is a Jew or a Greek. 2  This includes you, the reader. The Father loves His people so much that He calls them His children. 3  God's Holy Spirit makes believers God's adopted children, so believers call God Abba, which means Father. As God's children, believers will also inherit what God has promised. 4  God marks believers with the promised Holy Spirit, who guarantees that inheritance. 5  Until Christ returns, believers struggle against principalities and powers, the rebel rulers in the heavenly places. 6  Yet none of these powers can cut believers off from God's love in Christ Jesus. 7
1 Jhn 1:12 2 Gal 3:26-28 3 1Jn 3:1 4 Rom 8:15-17 5 Eph 1:13-14 6 Eph 6:12 7 Rom 8:38-39

headings.name: The revealing of the sons of God

columns.text: The adopted sons of God are not yet seen for who they are. All creation is waiting eagerly for the day when God reveals His sons. 1  When Christ appears, believers will be like Christ. 2  Those who stayed faithful to Christ will live and reign with Him. 3  The prophet Daniel saw that God would give the kingdom to His holy people. 4  God gave Adam rule over the earth, and Adam lost it. 5  Now the sons of God in Christ receive the kingdom.
1 Rom 8:19 2 1Jn 3:2 3 Rev 20:4 4 Dan 7:27 5 Gen 1:28

headings.name: One family of the sons of God

columns.text: The story ends where God always meant it to end. God makes His home with His people on a renewed earth, 1 and His people see His face. 2  The tree of life, which Adam lost in Eden, stands again in God's garden, called Paradise. 3  God's whole family in heaven and on earth takes its name from God, 4 and that family is gathered into one in Christ, just as God planned before the world began. 5
1 Rev 21:1-3 2 Rev 22:4 3 Rev 2:7 4 Eph 3:15 5 Eph 1:10

pages.title: Feasts of God: Timing of Yahweh

headings.name: His appointed times

columns.text: Long ago, after God, whose personal name is Yahweh, brought the people of Israel out of slavery in Egypt, Yahweh gave them a calendar of seven yearly feasts. A feast was a holy day or week when the people stopped their ordinary work and gathered to worship. Yahweh called these feasts His own appointed times, set days for holy convocations. 1 Four feasts fell in spring and early summer, and three fell in autumn. This page walks through the feasts in the order of the year. Like the pictures in a stained-glass window, the feasts show what Yahweh is doing in history. The apostle Paul says the feasts are a shadow of things to come, and that the reality is found in Christ. 2 The spring feasts point to what Christ has already done. The autumn feasts point to what is still to come. The stained-glass picture is from hisfinishedwork.com, chapter 4 Takeaways. :::info The seven feasts at a glance 1. Passover: first month, fourteenth day. Lev 23:5 2. Unleavened Bread: first month, fifteenth day, for seven days. Lev 23:6 3. Firstfruits: the day after the Sabbath. Lev 23:10-11 4. Weeks (Pentecost): fifty days later. Lev 23:15-16 5. Trumpets: seventh month, first day. Lev 23:24 6. Day of Atonement: seventh month, tenth day. Lev 23:27 7. Tabernacles: seventh month, fifteenth day, for seven days. Lev 23:34
1 Lev 23:2 2 Col 2:16-17

headings.name: Spring: what has been fulfilled

columns.text: The first feast is Passover. On the night Yahweh freed Israel from Egypt, each family killed a lamb and painted its blood on the doorframe of the house. When Yahweh saw the blood, He passed over that house and spared it. 1  Yahweh did not let the destroyer enter the houses marked with blood. 2  Paul calls Christ the Passover lamb, sacrificed for His people. 3  A sacrifice was an animal killed in worship to deal with sin. People made right with God through Christ's blood will be saved from God's anger through Christ. 4
1 Exo 12:13 2 Exo 12:23 3 1Co 5:7 4 Rom 5:9

The Feast of Unleavened Bread began the day after Passover and lasted seven days. Leaven is yeast, which makes dough rise. Israel left Egypt in such haste that their bread had no time to rise. 1  Paul uses leaven as a picture of sin that spreads through a whole life. Paul tells believers to clear out the old leaven of malice and wickedness and to keep the feast with honesty and truth. 2
1 Exo 12:39 2 1Co 5:7-8

The Feast of Firstfruits came on the day after the Sabbath, the weekly day of rest. When the harvest began, the priest waved the first sheaf of grain before Yahweh. 1  Christ rose from the dead as the firstfruits, the first of all who have died to be raised, and a sign that the rest will follow. 2
1 Lev 23:10-11 2 1Co 15:20

The Feast of Weeks came fifty days after Firstfruits, so the feast is also called Pentecost, from the Greek word for fiftieth. Israel counted the fifty days and then brought a new offering of grain to Yahweh. 1  Long before, Israel had reached Mount Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt, 2 and Yahweh came down on the mountain in fire, with the sound of a trumpet, to give Israel His law. 3  When the Day of Pentecost came after Jesus rose from the dead, God's Holy Spirit came on Jesus' followers with something like flames of fire. 4  Yahweh had promised that one day He would write His law on His people's hearts. 5  Paul says the Spirit writes on human hearts, not on tablets of stone like the law at Sinai. 6  Scripture does not tie Sinai or the heart-written law to the day of Pentecost in so many words. That link is an Inference.
1 Lev 23:15-16 2 Exo 19:1 3 Exo 19:16-18 4 Act 2:1-4 5 Jer 31:33 6 2Co 3:3

headings.name: Autumn: what is still to come

columns.text: After the summer harvest came the autumn feasts. The Feast of Trumpets fell on the first day of the seventh month, a day of rest and remembrance marked by blowing trumpets. 1  Paul writes that the Lord Jesus Himself will come down from heaven with the sound of God's trumpet. 2  At the last trumpet the dead will be raised, never to decay again. 3  Scripture does not name these events as the fulfilment of the feast. The link is an inference drawn from the trumpet.
1 Lev 23:24 2 1Th 4:16 3 1Co 15:52

Ten days later came the Day of Atonement. Atonement means covering sin so that people can be made right with God. On this one day each year, the high priest went behind the veil, the curtain that closed off the innermost room of God's house, and the high priest always took blood with him. 1  The high priest also confessed Israel's sins over a live goat, and the goat carried those sins away into the wilderness. 2  Christ entered the Most Holy Place once, for all time, with His own blood. 3  The prophet Zechariah says Israel will one day look on the One they pierced and will mourn, 4 and a fountain will be opened to wash away their sin. 5  Zechariah does not name the Day of Atonement. The link is drawn from the mourning and cleansing.
1 Heb 9:7 2 Lev 16:21-22 3 Heb 9:12 4 Zec 12:10 5 Zec 13:1

Five days later came the Feast of Tabernacles, the last feast of the year. For seven days Israel lived in booths and rejoiced before Yahweh. 1  The booths reminded Israel of the shelters they lived in after Yahweh brought them out of Egypt. The Gospel of John says that Jesus, the Son of God, became a human being and lived among people, like God pitching His tent among them. 2  In the coming kingdom, the nations will go up to Jerusalem year by year to worship the King and keep the Feast of Tabernacles. 3  At the very end of the Bible, a loud voice from heaven announces that God now makes His home with people. 4
1 Lev 23:40-42 2 Jhn 1:14 3 Zec 14:16 4 Rev 21:3

headings.name: The calendar is the story

columns.text: So Israel's calendar tells the whole story in a single year. The year opens with a lamb's blood that saves God's people from death in Egypt, 1 and the year closes with a feast that remembers God bringing His people out to live with Him. 2  The Bible runs the same way, from God's rescue of His people to God living with His people forever on a renewed earth. 3
1 Exo 12:13 2 Lev 23:42-43 3 Rev 21:1-3

pages.title: The Kingdom of God: Fall and Rise

headings.name: Lost and given back

columns.text: This page sets the beginning of the Bible beside its end. In Genesis, the first book of the Bible, people lose one good thing after another: their home with God, a shared language, and life itself. In Revelation, the last book of the Bible, God gives each of those things back, and often gives back more than was lost. Each section below tells one loss, then tells how God reversed it.

headings.name: The garden lost, and the garden regained

columns.text: In the beginning God placed the first man and woman, Adam and Eve, in a garden called Eden, where the tree of life grew. 1 After Adam and Eve disobeyed God, God sent them out of the garden, and heavenly guards called cherubim, with a flaming sword, blocked the way back to the tree of life. 2
1 Gen 2:8-9 2 Gen 3:23-24

At the end of the Bible the way is open again. Jesus promises that everyone who stays faithful to the end will eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God. 1  The leaves of the tree of life bring healing to the nations, 2 and the gates of God's city are never shut. 3  The garden that was guarded is now open.
1 Rev 2:7 2 Rev 22:2 3 Rev 21:25

headings.name: Babel: language confused, and Pentecost: language heard

columns.text: After the great flood, the people of the earth all spoke one language. At a place called Babel they gathered to build a tower and make a name for themselves. God, whose personal name is Yahweh, confused their language so that they could not understand one another, and then Yahweh scattered them across the earth. 1  The Most High, a title of God as ruler over all nations, set the borders of the scattered nations according to the number of the sons of God, heavenly beings who serve God. 2  The ESV, an English translation, reads "sons of God" in this verse, following a Dead Sea Scroll and the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation. The NKJV follows the standard Hebrew text and reads "children of Israel". The divided nations were given the host of heaven as their portion, 3 and the nations served their own gods. 4
1 Gen 11:4-8 2 Deu 32:8 3 Deu 4:19 4 Deu 12:2

Many centuries later the scattering began to be undone. Pentecost was a yearly feast, when Jews from many nations gathered in Jerusalem. At Pentecost, after Jesus had risen from the dead and returned to heaven, God's Holy Spirit came on Jesus' disciples. Something like flames of fire rested on the disciples, and visitors from many nations each heard the disciples speaking in the visitors' own languages. 1  At Babel nobody could understand anyone else. 2  At Pentecost everybody understood. Through the prophet Zephaniah, Yahweh had promised to give the peoples pure speech so that they could all call on His name. 3  At the end of the story, a great crowd from every nation and language stands together before God's throne. 4
1 Act 2:3-6 2 Gen 11:7 3 Zep 3:9 4 Rev 7:9

headings.name: Sinai and Pentecost: three thousand

columns.text: After God brought Israel out of slavery in Egypt, Israel camped at Mount Sinai, where God gave them His law. While Moses, their leader, was on the mountain, the people made a golden calf and worshipped it as a god. 1  About three thousand men died that day as judgement. 2
1 Exo 32:8 2 Exo 32:28

At Pentecost, when God gave His Spirit, about three thousand people believed and were added to the followers of Jesus that day. 1  The law given at Sinai ended that day with three thousand dead. The Spirit given at Pentecost began with three thousand given new life. Paul explains that the written law brings death, but the Spirit gives life. 2
1 Act 2:41 2 2Co 3:6

headings.name: A name for themselves, and His name

columns.text: The builders at Babel wanted to make a name for themselves, so that people would remember and honour them. 1
1 Gen 11:4

Jesus did the opposite. Jesus did not seek a name for Himself but humbled Himself to the point of death on a cross, and God gave Jesus the name above every name. 1  At the end of the Bible, God's servants carry God's name on their foreheads. 2  The people who tried to make their own name were scattered, and the people who carry God's name are gathered.
1 Php 2:8-9 2 Rev 22:4

headings.name: A tower up to heaven, and a city down from heaven

columns.text: The builders at Babel wanted their tower to reach up into the heavens. 1  People were trying to climb up to God by their own effort.
1 Gen 11:4
At the end of the Bible the direction is reversed. The New Jerusalem, God's holy city, comes down out of heaven from God. 1  People could not climb up to heaven, so God comes down to them.
1 Rev 21:2

headings.name: One man's disobedience, and one Man's obedience

columns.text: The apostle Paul explains that sin came into the world through one man, Adam, and that death came with sin, so death spread to everyone. 1
1 Rom 5:12

Jesus is the second one man in Paul's story. Through the obedience of Jesus, many people are made right with God. 1  Just as all people die because of Adam, so all who belong to Christ will be made alive. 2
1 Rom 5:19 2 1Co 15:22

headings.name: Sons of God who rebelled, and sons of God revealed

columns.text: Before the great flood, heavenly beings called the sons of God took wives from among women on earth, 1 and the earth was filled with violence. 2
1 Gen 6:2 2 Gen 6:11

In the New Testament the title sons of God is given to a new family. All who believe are sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. 1  All creation is waiting eagerly for the day when God reveals these sons, and on that day creation itself will be set free. 2  The sons of God who rebelled filled the earth with violence. The sons of God in Christ will see the earth set free.
1 Gal 3:26 2 Rom 8:19-21

headings.name: The nations disinherited, and the nations inherited

columns.text: After Babel, the Most High, a title of God as ruler over all nations, divided the nations according to the number of the sons of God and kept the people of Jacob, Israel, as His own portion. 1  The ESV reads "sons of God" in this verse, following a Dead Sea Scroll and the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation. The NKJV follows the standard Hebrew text and reads "children of Israel". So every nation except Israel was handed over to other powers.
1 Deu 32:8-9

The nations are not lost forever. Psalm 82 ends by asking God to rise up and judge the earth, because all the nations belong to God. 1  At the end of the Bible, the nations walk in the light of the New Jerusalem. 2  The nations that were handed over at Babel are welcomed home.
1 Psa 82:8 2 Rev 21:24

headings.name: The curse, and no more curse

columns.text: After Adam disobeyed, God cursed the ground. The ground would grow thorns and thistles, people would toil for their food, and every person would die and return to dust. 1
1 Gen 3:17-19

Jesus, the King God promised, wore a crown of thorns when soldiers mocked Him before His death. 1  Paul says Jesus became a curse by being hung on a tree, the cross, to free His people from the curse of the law. 2  At the end of the Bible there is no more curse 3 and no more death. 4
1 Mat 27:29 2 Gal 3:13 3 Rev 22:3 4 Rev 21:4

headings.name: Glory departed, and God with us

columns.text: In Eden, God walked in the garden where the first people lived. 1  Later God lived among Israel in the temple in Jerusalem. When Israel kept worshipping idols, the glory of Yahweh, the visible sign of God's presence, left the temple. 2
1 Gen 3:8 2 Ezk 10:18
Jesus was called Immanuel, which means God with us. 1  At the end of the Bible, God makes His home with people on a renewed earth, 2 and they see His face. 3
1 Mat 1:23 2 Rev 21:1-3 3 Rev 22:4

headings.name: Eden to Eden

columns.text: So the story ends where it began, only better. The story began with Yahweh God walking in a garden where the first man and woman lived. 1  The story ends with God living among His people forever, 2 with the tree of life growing in the middle of God's city. 3
1 Gen 3:8 2 Rev 21:3 3 Rev 22:2
